_comment: Curated models.dev MetadataID -> entity-tuple OVERRIDE table for the metadata<->entity join (metadata_join.go). It is consulted FIRST and takes PRECEDENCE over the mechanical decomposition (curated > mechanical, matching the parse/ curated-overrides and ollama_aliases.json precedents). A models.dev metadata id is lab-scoped ('<lab>/<model>', e.g. 'zhipuai/glm-4.6'); the mechanical join strips the '<lab>/' prefix, decomposes the remainder through the production parse pipeline (ParseFamilyDetailed + ParseParamSize) into an EntityRef key, and matches that key against the catalog entity set. An alias is needed precisely where the mechanical key MISSES the catalog (family present but tuple mismatch -> otherwise reported in modelsdev_unlinked.json) or matches the WRONG entity, so the curator can re-map the metadata id onto the intended identity. KEYING: keys are lowercased MetadataID strings. Each value is an explicit entity tuple: 'family' (canonical, lowercase), optional 'variant', optional 'version', optional 'param_size' (canonical ParseParamSize token, e.g. '70b'), and optional 'modifier' (the IDENTITY-class modifier list, EntityModifiers projection). Keys MUST be kept sorted. This file is hand-curated seed data; no tool rewrites it. Example row shape (illustrative, not active): "somelab/some-model-70b": {"family": "llama", "version": "3.3", "param_size": "70b", "modifier": ["instruct"]}. COLLISION HAZARD — before aliasing, verify the target is a DISTINCT entity: do NOT alias a metadata id onto an entity that already carries another row's metadata or that conflates several distinct lab models under one coarse key, because the last write wins and aliasing then silently OVERWRITES or MISATTRIBUTES metadata. NOTE: the v0.2.5 stage/mode identity work gave the previously-coarse forms their own distinct entities — gemini-omni-flash-preview -> gemini/flash{omni}, gpt-realtime-2.1 -> gpt@2.1, and laguna xs/m -> laguna/xs and laguna/m — so the three rows once left unaliasable in modelsdev_unlinked.json now attach: the gpt/gemini rows MECHANICALLY (their lab-stripped ids hit the serving idFamilyOverrides), and the three laguna rows via the aliases below (poolside is both the lab AND the serving provider, so the join strips 'poolside/' and the mechanical remainder alone would miss the sized xs/m variant).
